title: How to use Linear for designers on Mac: managing creative tasks effectively
metaTitle: Linear for designers on Mac: workflow tips for creative teams
description: Learn to manage design tasks in Linear on Mac. Get tips on keyboard shortcuts, issue tracking, and using Lazur to keep your creative focus sharp.
intro: Linear for designers on Mac helps you track creative work without breaking your flow. Many designers struggle to keep their project management tools updated while maintaining deep work blocks.
tldr: Linear is a keyboard-first tool that works well for design teams on macOS.
The desktop app for Mac requires macOS 12 or later.
Designers can use the command palette to quickly create or update design tasks.
Lazur helps you navigate Linear by answering questions and pointing to specific UI elements.
Use keyboard shortcuts to minimize mouse usage and protect your creative time.

blocks.text: Why designers choose Linear on Mac

Linear is popular with designers because it feels fast. It avoids the heavy interface of older project management tools. On a Mac, the desktop app provides a clean experience that stays out of your way. You can download the installer directly from their website. It runs on both Apple silicon and Intel chips.

The core of the experience is the keyboard. Designers who learn the shortcuts save time. Instead of clicking through menus, you use the command palette. Press ⌘K to open it. From there, you can create new issues, move tasks, or search for files. This helps you keep your hands on the keyboard while you work.
Mastering Linear keyboard shortcuts for designers

Linear relies on single-key shortcuts. These are designed to be intuitive. Press C to create an issue. Press P to set a priority level. Press ? to see the full list of shortcuts inside the app. If you forget one, Lazur can show you where it is.

items: C: Create a new issue quickly.
⌘K: Open the command menu for all actions.
P: Set priority for an issue.
G then I: Navigate to your inbox.
Shift + D: Set a due date for a task.

blocks.text: Designers need deep focus. Administrative work often interrupts this. Use Linear to batch your updates. Do not check your tasks every hour. Set aside specific times to clear your inbox. This keeps your creative momentum high during the day.
Use the command palette to search for your current project. This prevents you from getting lost in the sidebar. Keep your active tasks in a custom view to see only what matters now.
blocks.title: Stay focused

items: Trying to customize Linear like Jira. It is better to follow their opinionated workflow.
Manually updating tasks instead of using integrations with GitHub or Slack.
Ignoring the command palette and relying only on the mouse.
Creating too many teams early on, which makes tracking issues harder.

blocks.text: Many teams try to force Linear to be something it is not. It works best when you embrace its cycle-based system. If you need complex cross-departmental reporting, you might find it limited. For pure design and engineering tasks, it is hard to beat.

faq.question: Can I use Linear offline on my Mac?
faq.answer: Linear requires an internet connection to sync your data. It does not have a full offline mode.

faq.question: Does Linear have a native Mac app?
faq.answer: Yes, there is a desktop app for macOS. You can download it directly from the Linear website.

faq.question: How do I learn all the keyboard shortcuts?
faq.answer: Press the ? key inside the Linear app to view the complete list of shortcuts.
